#en: Somebody wiped this place lazy, like they trusted time to finish the job. Half the terminals still think it is three years ago, half the cameras loop blank corridors, and the security daemon is chasing ghosts in its own logs. I was supposed to audit a simple breach trail, tick the boxes, bill whoever hired me. Instead I find a chain of connection requests that never should have routed through a backwater lab like this, all handshakes half completed, then neatly severed just before they reached the main archive. Ran them through my own rig, out of habit, and every one of those broken calls resolves toward the same patch of deep nothing a dead coordinate buried under layers of "temporary" redirects. It feels too clean to be an accident, too convenient to be just fear. Whoever she is, she knew exactly how much to cut so the system would keep limping along, and now I am holding the first clean vector to wherever she sends the people who do not want to wait in line anymore.
zh: 有人把这地方擦得很懒散，像是笃定时间会替他们收尾。一半的终端还以为现在是三年前，一半的摄像头在空走廊里循环播放，安全守护进程在自己的日志里追着鬼跑。我本该审计一条简单的入侵痕迹，勾完表格，然后向雇我的人开账单。可我找到的却是一串本不该经过这么个穷乡实验室的连接请求，握手全都进行到一半就被干净利落地切断，正好在够到主档案之前。出于习惯，我把它们放进自己的机器里跑了一遍，结果那些中断的呼叫每一个都指向同一片深深的虚无——一个被层层"临时"重定向埋住的死坐标。这干净得不像意外，方便得不像单纯的恐惧。不管她是谁，她清楚该切掉多少，好让系统继续一瘸一拐地跑下去；如今我手里攥着第一条干净的矢量，通往她把那些不愿再排队等候的人送去的地方。

#en:
I should not be down here alone.

The pod still thinks it has a purpose. Consoles cycle through the same old sweeps on dead satellites, query beacons that have not answered in years, ping corridors UC stopped admitting existed. Nobody ever shut any of it off; they just stopped looking at the results. That is the only reason I found it. Buried in the rolling diagnostics, under three generations of "do not touch" tags, there is a route offset that repeats whenever one particular transponder pattern passes through the field. Cross-checking it against the fragments I pulled from that hillside cache, and the static-riddled jump data from the freighter that never arrived, it all lines up.  

Somewhere above this rock, between here and that stretch of wreck-strewn dark everyone pretends is just bad luck, the same tiny correction keeps being applied to ships that bought a certain kind of chart. The system is still nudging them, long after the people who set it up walked away.
zh:
我不该一个人待在这下面。

这个舱体还以为自己有用。控制台一遍遍对死去的卫星做着同样老旧的扫描，查询多年没应答过的信标，向联殖早已不再承认存在的航道发延时探测。从没人把这些关掉；他们只是不再看结果了。而这就是我唯一的发现途径。在滚动的诊断数据里，压在三代人留下的"勿动"标签底下，有一处航路偏移——每当某种特定的应答器波形经过这片空域，它就会重复出现。把它和我从山坡缓存里取出的碎片、以及那艘从未抵达的货船上满是静电的跃迁数据交叉比对，全部对得上。

在这块岩石上方的某处，从这里到那片人人都假装只是运气不好的残骸遍布的黑暗之间，同样那点微小的修正一直在被施加给那些买了某种星图的飞船。设置它的人早已离开，可系统仍在轻推着它们。

#en: I am writing this from the Riftblade, and the ship feels like it is trying to forget something. Drives are cold, power throttled down, but every bulkhead has that faint shiver you get after a hard abort, like the metal remembers being somewhere it should not have been. The manifest I am digging for should be routine cargo nonsense, but the routing stamps do not match the stories I heard back on the fringe. Same captain name, different paths. Same ports, different dates. Like someone took a perfectly straight haul and bent it just enough to slip between patrol sweeps. What gets me is how every step that led here was small, harmless on its own: a garbled ping from a monitoring shack, a miner talking about a missing cousin over cheap Erdebrau, a scratched-out line on an old service log. None of it screamed conspiracy, just little scuffs on the paint of reality, and somehow all of those quiet mistakes pushed me toward this dead ship and the name everybody swears they do not know.
zh: 我在裂刃号上写下这些，这艘船感觉像在努力忘记什么。驱动是冷的，功率被压到最低，可每块舱壁都带着那种硬着陆中止后才会有的微弱战栗，像金属记得自己去过本不该去的地方。我要挖的那份清单本该是些例行公事的货物废话，可航路戳记跟我在外缘听说的事对不上。同样的船长名，不同的路径。同样的港口，不同的日期。像是有人把一趟笔直的运输稍微掰弯，刚好够从巡逻扫描的缝隙里滑过去。真正让我在意的是，一路把我引到这里来的每一步都那么小、单看都无害：一座监测棚传来的含糊延时探测、一个矿工就着廉价埃尔德啤酒念叨失踪的表亲、一份旧维修日志上一行被划掉的字。没有一样像是阴谋，只是现实漆面上的小小擦痕；可不知怎的，所有这些安静的错误把我推向了这艘死船，以及那个人人都赌咒说自己不认识的名字。

#en: They say if you stay too long in a dead GalBank hull, you start hearing old transactions whisper in the bulkheads. Sitting in the cold server bay of this vault ship, watching the power flicker over racks nobody is supposed to know about, I almost believe it. The logs do not match the public story; course changes are shaved by fractions, storm alerts delayed by minutes, payouts denied on worlds that should have been safe. I have heard this tale in bars and supply queues, passed around like a ghost story about a nav engineer who tilted the sky, but every retelling trims an edge, blurs a name, makes it sound like bad luck instead of design. Out at that first backwater homestead, all I saw were ruined fields and people who cursed the weather; at the old listening post, I found recordings cut off mid-warning. Now the patterns in these sealed ledgers say none of it was random, and that someone has been very careful about which parts of the truth survive the trip to the next backroom.
zh: 都说你要是在一具死去的盖尔银行船壳里待得太久，就会开始听见旧交易在舱壁里低语。坐在这种金库船的冰冷服务器舱里，看着没人该知道的机架上电力忽明忽暗，我几乎信了。日志与对外的说法对不上；航向被削掉几分之几度，风暴警报被延迟几分钟，本该安全的世界却被拒付赔款。我在酒吧和补给队列里听过这个故事，它被传来传去，像一则关于某个把天空掰斜的导航工程师的鬼故事；可每次转述都会剪掉一个棱角、模糊一个名字，让它听起来像运气不好，而不是精心设计。在那第一座穷乡农庄，我看到的只有毁掉的田地和咒骂天气的人；在旧监听站，我找到的录音在警告中途就被切断。如今这些密封账簿里的图案说明，这一切都不是随机的；有人非常小心地决定，真相的哪些部分才被允许活着走进下一个后堂。

#en:
I picked up that dataslate because Rafi swore Juno swore her cousin had pulled it off a dead hauler out near Narion. That is how it always goes out here. No one ever finds anything themselves, they just pass along someone else's ghosts.

I ran the file on my bunk, lights low, just the hum of the recycler and that cold glow on my hands.

Course data, stamped like it came off a UC console twenty years ago, but nudging jumps by half a degree here, a full degree there.

Nothing dramatic, just a slow drift.

When I asked Rafi where Juno's cousin actually got it, he laughed and said he heard it from a Ranger who heard it from a smuggler who heard it from a Navy washout.

Every name was a step sideways, never forward.

Now I am sitting in a ship that hums the same way, staring at routes that look just a little too clean, and all I can think is that whatever started this never had to show its face.

It just needed people like us, trusting that somebody else checked the math.
zh:
我捡起那块数据板，是因为拉菲赌咒说朱诺赌咒说她表亲从纳里昂附近一艘死货船上弄来的。在这外面事情从来都是这样。没人自己找到过任何东西，大家只是转手传递别人的鬼。

我在铺位上跑那份文件，灯光调暗，只有回收机在嗡鸣，冷光落在手上。

航路数据，戳记像二十年前从联殖控制台上打出来的，却把跃迁一处拧偏半度、一处拧偏整整一度。

没什么戏剧性，只是缓慢的漂移。

我问拉菲，朱诺的表亲到底是从哪儿弄来的，他笑了，说他是从一个游骑兵那儿听来的，游骑兵又是从一个走私贩那儿，走私贩又是从一个海军淘汰兵那儿听来的。

每个名字都是一步横向偏移，从来不是向前。

如今我坐在一条以同样方式嗡鸣的飞船里，盯着那些看起来稍微太干净了一点的航线，满脑子只有一个念头：挑起这一切的东西，从来不必露面。

它只需要我们这样的人，信任别人已经核对过算式。

#en:
I always thought banks were boring, even when they were floating in orbit. Turns out the quiet ones hide the worst rot.  

I have been on this derelict for three hours now, lungs full of recycled dust and old insulation, watching GalBank headers scroll past on dead consoles. The numbers say traffic, insurance, expected loss. Between the lines, I see ships nudged a little off the lanes, like someone was leaning on the galaxy with one finger. Nobody flagged it. Nobody wanted to.  

Out in that first backwater outpost, the locals just shrugged when routes shifted, said the sky changes. Later, that beacon in orbit with its jittery telemetry seemed like a one-off glitch. Now, buried in this courier's belly, I can feel the pattern tightening, realize how long this has been in the system, ignored because it was profitable to look away. Whatever I pull from here points toward Neon, toward high steel where someone has been rewriting how we travel while the rest of us pretend not to notice.
zh:
我一直以为银行很无聊，哪怕它们漂在轨道上。结果发现，安静的那种才藏着最烂的腐坏。

我在这艘弃船上待了三个小时了，肺里灌满再循环的灰尘和旧隔热层，看着盖尔银行的页眉在死控制台上滚过。那些数字说的是交通、保险、预期损失。可我在字里行间看见飞船被轻轻推离航道，像有人用一根手指压着银河。没人标记它。没人想标记。

在那第一座穷乡前哨站，航线一变，本地人只是耸耸肩，说天空会变。后来，轨道上那座遥测抖个不停的信标，看起来像一次性的故障。如今，埋在这艘快船肚子里，我能感觉到那图案正在收紧，意识到它在这套系统里已经存在了多久——一直被忽视，因为别过头去是有利可图的。我从这里挖出的任何东西都指向霓虹城，指向那些高耸的钢铁，那里有人在改写我们出行的方式，而我们其余人假装没看见。

#en: I signed on to Heat Ridge because it was supposed to be simple work. Guard duty, they said. Easy credits babysitting a dead UC husk no one remembered filing the decommission papers for. First few months it really was that dull; same patrol routes on half-lit catwalks, same hum of old scanners sweeping an empty sky out of habit. Felt like we were watching a locked door in a corridor no one walked anymore.\n\nThen the captain started checking the sensor room himself. Not just once, but every shift change. We got told not to touch certain consoles, not to ask why the old arrays were suddenly drawing more power. The logs started filling up with tiny course corrections for ships that, on paper, never passed within a system of us. No alarms, no flags, just little numbers pushed into folders marked routine. Somewhere along the way, standing post on a forgotten station turned into sitting on something someone else did not want found, and none of us could say when that change actually happened.
zh: 我签下热脊的任务，是因为它本该是份简单活儿。他们说是站岗。轻松挣信用币，照看一具没人记得提交过退役文件的联殖死壳。头几个月确实就那么无聊；半亮的天桥上同样的巡逻路线，老扫描仪出于习惯扫着同一片空荡天空，发出同样的嗡鸣。感觉就像我们在看守一条再没人走的走廊里一扇锁着的门。\n\n后来，船长开始亲自检查传感器室。不是一次，而是每个交班都去。我们被告知不许碰某些控制台，不许问为什么那些老旧阵列突然开始耗更多电。日志里开始填满些微小的航向修正，对象是那些纸面上从未经过我们所在星系范围内的飞船。没有警报，没有标记，只有一些小数字被塞进标着"例行"的文件夹。不知不觉间，在一座被遗忘的空间站上站岗，变成了坐守某样别人不愿被找到的东西；而我们谁都说不上来，这变化究竟是什么时候发生的。

#en: I keep replaying that day the crate lists, the loader jams, and suddenly we are staring at seals with medical hazard glyphs instead of processed grain. Trade Authority paperwork said "nutritional supplements." Smelled like antiseptic and metal, the way every battlefield clinic I have ever limped through smells. Jonas cracked a joke, Kira logged it under a different code, Elias just went very, very quiet. No one wanted to say the obvious out loud that somebody was shunting chems to places that do not show up on any of our route maps. Since then, every time some spacer in the dockside bar mutters about a ghost medic patching up people the system forgot, the crew shifts in their seats. They laugh it off, look at their drinks or the wall or anything that is not my face. Manifest says we jumped clean from Gagarin, but the nav buffer shows a burned-in echo of a different vector, a short, dirty hop toward nowhere. The closer I look, the more the gaps line up into a shape that feels like intent.
zh: 那天的事我一直在脑子里重放：货箱清单、装卸机卡住，然后我们忽然盯着一堆印着医疗危险符号的封条，而不是加工好的谷物。贸易管理局的文件上写着"营养补充剂"。那气味像消毒剂和金属，就像我拖着腿进过的每一间战地诊所的味道。乔纳斯说了个笑话，基拉把它记到了另一个代码下，伊莱亚斯只是变得非常、非常安静。没人愿意把显而易见的话说出口——有人正在把药剂转运到任何一个航图上都不显示的地方。从那以后，每当码头酒吧里哪个太空人嘟囔起一个给系统遗忘之人疗伤的幽灵军医，船员们就在座位上挪动身体。他们一笑带过，盯着自己的酒、盯着墙，盯着任何不是我的脸的东西。清单说我们是从加加林干净地跃过来的，可导航缓冲里却留着一道另一条矢量的烙痕，一次朝虚无的短促而肮脏的跳转。我看得越仔细，那些空白就越拼成一个像是"有意为之"的形状。

#en: I keep replaying that intake shift in my head. One overworked Trade Authority clerk, three screens blinking orange, and a cargo ship with a routing anomaly that "looked like a sensor hiccup." Nobody wanted to hold the line over a few mismatched timestamps when there were paying haulers stacked behind it. We cleared Tidewalker TA-7207 with a shrug and a shared joke about phantom paperwork, and I told myself I would circle back to the discrepancy after shift. I did not.\n\nSince then I have watched settlement distress calls pile up from worlds stamped "marginal but viable," watched survey signatures come through with tiny calibration quirks that feel familiar now. The stories all sound the same: storms no model mentioned, groundwater souring overnight, coordinates bought from someone who swore the numbers were solid. One skipped follow-up turned into a corridor nobody questioned, the perfect place for a man who lives in the blind spots between what the data says and what people want to believe.
zh: 那个接收窗口的班我一直在脑子里重放。一个忙不过来的贸易管理局文员，三块屏幕闪着橙色，还有一艘货船的航路异常"看着像传感器打嗝"。后面还排着付了钱的运货船员，谁愿意为几个对不上的时间戳卡住队伍呢。我们耸耸肩，开了个关于幽灵文书工作的玩笑，就把潮行者 TA-7207 放行了，我还告诉自己交班后回头再查那处出入。我没查。\n\n从那以后，我看着盖着"边缘但可行"印章的星球不断累积起定居者的求救呼叫，看着勘测签名带着如今感觉很眼熟的那些微小校准怪癖传进来。那些故事听起来都一样：模型从未提及的风暴、一夜之间变酸的地下水、从某个赌咒说数据可靠的人手里买来的坐标。一次被跳过的跟进，变成了一条无人质疑的走廊——对那种活"数据所说的"与"人们愿意相信的"之间盲区里的人而言，这是完美的藏身处。

#en: I keep telling myself I am not paranoid, just observant. Then I look around this box they call a command post and see how every wall is held up by things no one wants to say out loud. Manifests pinned under other manifests, patrol reports with whole hours missing, hauler complaints tagged "resolved" when I know damn well no one even sent a reply. Today I found three different versions of the same convoy's route, all stamped clean. Only the timing lines did not match. Little delays, a few seconds here, a minute there, always bending the same way. When I traced them on the board they curved into something like a spiral, neat as you please. I asked dispatch about it and got silence, then too much talking about unrelated sectors. Everyone pretended not to understand which files I meant, like we were all suddenly bad at our jobs at the same time. That is when I knew this was bigger than a bad routing algorithm and that whatever is sitting at the center of that spiral is not supposed to have a name.
zh: 我一直告诉自己我不是多疑，只是善于观察。然后我环顾这间他们称作指挥所的盒子，看见每一面墙都是靠没人愿意说出口的东西撑着的。清单压在别的清单底下，巡逻报告整小时整小时地缺失，运货船员的投诉被标成"已解决"，而我他妈的清楚根本没人回过一句。今天我找到同一支运输队路线的三个不同版本，全都盖着干净的章。只有时间线对不上。小小的延迟，这里几秒，那里一分钟，永远朝同一个方向弯。我在图板上把它们描出来，它们就弯成了一个螺旋似的东西，整整齐齐。我去问调度，得到的先是沉默，然后是一大堆关于无关星区的废话。人人都假装听不懂我说的是哪些文件，就像我们忽然同时变得不会干活了。那一刻我就知道，这比一个糟糕的航路算法大得多；而坐在那螺旋中心的东西，本不该有名字。

#en: I have been staring at these screens long enough that the afterimage of the graphs follows me when I close my eyes. No windows down here, just recycled air and the low whine of processors chewing on data no one officially collects anymore. Off the record, half the bureau will tell you they have heard of "those routes" in a bar somewhere between shifts. On duty, those same people swear the charts are clean, the lanes are safe, and any missing tonnage is bad bookkeeping or pirate work. Funny how the stories thin out when the recorder is running.\n\nI pulled a jump log from a small freighter that never arrived, overlaid it with half-erased telemetry from an old survey corridor, and there it was again: that same tiny course correction, like a hand on the rudder just off-center. Someone built that into the system, then everyone agreed not to see it. Whatever this cartographer is doing, it is stitched straight into the gap between what we know in private and what we are allowed to write in the report.
zh: 我盯着这些屏幕太久，一闭眼那些图表的残影就跟着我。这下面没有窗户，只有再循环的空气和处理器低低的呜咽——它们在嚼着官方早已不再收集的数据。私下里，半个局子的人都会告诉你，他们在交班间隙的某个酒吧里听说过"那些航线"。可一到当班时，同样是这些人却赌咒说星图是干净的、航道是安全的，任何失踪的吨位都只是记账太糟或海盗干的。好笑的是，只要录音机一开，那些故事就都变稀薄了。\n\n我调出一艘从未抵达的小货船的跃迁日志，把它和一条旧勘测走廊里擦了一半的遥测叠在一起，它又出现了：同样那点微小的航向修正，像一只手把舵稍稍推离了中心。有人把它建进了系统，然后所有人一致同意不去看见它。不管这位制图师在做什么，它被直接缝进了"我们私下知道什么"与"我们被允许写进报告什么"之间的那道缝隙里。
